note: A UI-correctness release, from the 26 Aug tester batch. Opening a saved run no longer destroys the charts of the flight you were looking at — that one line is where everyone's duplicate history rows came from — and any other saved run of the design on screen can have its plots redrawn without adding a row. Save As opens a real save dialog on Chrome and Edge (it never did on any browser; files went silently to Downloads under the rocket's name, which read as overwriting the file you opened), and names the file it wrote everywhere else. The aerodynamics model is now a switch in the vitals strip, session-scoped and never writing your preference, and switching it marks the flight you were looking at instead of discarding it. The Design canvas stopped pushing the page off the bottom of the screen, the notice bar stopped sitting on the footer, every download button names its data rather than its format, and a version indicator beside the badge answers 'am I on the current version?' against what is actually deployed. Turning the first-run tour off works. Mass added to an overridden stage is no longer a silent no-op — the first of the two limits stated in 0.073. And a saved .ork now carries the flight results we computed, for configurations whose design, motors and conditions have not changed since the run.
